..
Issued at 530 AM EDT Mon Sep 14 2026

Cooler and dry today, with calm winds this morning strengthening out 
of the east-southeast through the day. Highs will be in the 70s. 
Patchy ground fog is possible this morning. Winds shift south-
southwest this evening into Tuesday morning with gusts up to around 
25-30 mph on/along Lake MI, so have a small craft advisory for both 
of our marine zones. We have a moderate swim risk for beaches along 
the Berrien County, MI shoreline on Tuesday as winds shift southwest 
and waves build to 2-3 feet (highest further north). A strong 
longshore current flowing from south to north along the beaches is 
likely, in addition to strong structural currents near piers and 
breakwalls (especially the south sides). Rip currents are possible. 

Surface high pressure sprawled across the Great Lakes today will 
slowly shift eastward to the east coast by Tuesday afternoon. The 
upper level ridge will remain anchored over the SE CONUS, extending 
northward today into the Great Lakes before taking on a more SW to 
NE tilt through Tuesday. Meanwhile, an upper level low and surface 
low pressure system drift through the Canadian Prairies/northern 
plains and into Quebec/Hudson Bay/James Bay through Tuesday night. 
The subsequent upper level trough reaches down into MN/WI/MI by Tue 
afternoon, breaking down/shifting our ridge east so we are left with 
relatively zonal flow through at least Thursday. At the surface, the 
cold front extends down from northern Ontario (Tue AM) into IA/IL/MO 
(occluding further north in WI/Upper MI). The warm front is draped 
from down from WI through IL/TN/KY at the same time. Return flow 
around the exiting surface high will pull up warm, moist air from 
the gulf into our forecast area through the morning/afternoon hours. 
The cold front arrives on our western doorstep by Tue evening, 
shifting east-southeast overnight before becoming stationary/diffuse 
Wed AM.  For now, have pops in the 20-50 percent range for late 
tonight (far west near Lake MI) and Tuesday morning, expanding 
slightly east and lingering on our northern CWA through the 
afternoon. Some of the model guidance brings the warm front up and 
starts rain showers/isolated storms earlier Tuesday, then we have a 
quick break and chances increase again late afternoon/early evening 
further west along Lake MI near the cold front. Others keep any warm 
front precip further northeast out of our area, so it's possible Tue 
is mostly dry (some of these models also slightly slower with the 
front). Have 20-50% chances until the early evening hours (highest 
north and west), and then increase chances to 40-80% after that as 
the front enters the CWA and stalls out. Severe weather potential 
depends on what happens in the earlier part of the day Tue, and then 
on the front timing and strength in the evening (some slight height 
rises still that could limit intensity, especially further SE). If 
we can keep building instability through the day and the cold front 
arrives in the late afternoon/early evening, we could see isolated 
severe storms with damaging wind gusts. Instability could be as high 
as 2000 J/kg (MLCAPE), with 20-30 knots of 0-6 km bulk shear 
(slightly higher further north in MI). Confidence is still pretty 
low, as mid level lapse rates are pretty crummy (5-6 C/km), there is 
potential for mid-level height rises that could limit intensity 
(front becomes more diffuse with time), and impacts from earlier 
daytime showers or storms (if they happen) could make the 
environment less favorable overall. SPC still has our area in a 
marginal risk for severe weather occurring. High temperatures on 
Tuesday could reach into the upper 80s, low 90s west of I 69 and 
further south. A lot will depend on whether we have cloud 
debris/morning rain or storms that limit the daytime heating. It 
will also be more humid than today. 

The front stalls/washes out and we have zonal flow aloft through 
Thursday...which makes us susceptible to various shortwaves that 
move through. The stationary boundary does lift northward a bit as 
warm air advects in from the south again, eventually orienting it 
from NE MO into north central IL, NW IN, and southern Lower MI. This 
keeps around 30-60% chances for rain and thunderstorm activity until 
Thursday. Highs will be in the 70s, low-mid 80s for most days. 

Low chances for showers and storms continue through the weekend (20-
30%), with highs in the 70s, low 80s.
